title: Feed A Crowd: Mexican Bean and Potato Bake
subtitle: Cook Once, Serve More!
description: Serve up more with our Feed A Crowd recipes! Using more hearty ingredients like filling carbs, proteins and veggies, you can satisfy extra hungry tummies or keep something for tomorrow’s lunch. If you’re on a 2-person plan, these recipes make 4 portions; on a 4-person plan, they make 8 portions.

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Preheat the oven to 220C, fan-forced. Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil for the potatoes. Peel the potatoes, then cut into 3mm-thick slices with a mandoline or sharp knife (see Feed A Crowd). Cut the carrots into 1cm chunks. Finely chop the onion. Crush or finely chop 2 garlic cloves. Coarsely grate the cheese. Drain and rinse the beans.

Cook potato: Cook the potato in the pan of boiling water for 5 mins or until tender. Reserve 375ml (1½ cups) cooking water, then drain the potato and refresh under cold running water. Meanwhile, heat 1½ tbs olive oil in a large deep frypan over medium heat. Cook the carrot and onion, stirring regularly, for 7 mins or until softened.

Simmer beans: Add the garlic, 1 tbs Mexican spice blend (see Feed A Crowd) and 2 tbs tomato paste to the veggies and cook, stirring, for 1 min or until fragrant. Add the beans, tomatoes, reserved cooking water and 1 tbs barbecue sauce and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to medium and cook, covered, for 5 mins or until slightly thickened.

Assemble bake: Remove the pan from the heat. Taste, then season with salt and pepper. Grease a 3L (12 cup) baking dish. Arrange one-third of the potato slices over the base of the dish. Top with the bean mixture, then arrange the remaining potato slices over the top, overlapping one another. Spray or brush with olive oil, season with salt and pepper and scatter over the cheese.
Bake and serve up: Bake for 15 mins or until golden. Divide the bean and potato bake among plates or pop the dish on the table for everyone to help themselves. Enjoy!

Feed A Crowd: Prefer mash instead? Cut the peeled potatoes into 2cm chunks and boil for 10 mins or until tender. Drain, then add a little butter and milk and mash until smooth. Top the bean mixture with the mash, scatter over the cheese and bake until golden. ~ Our Mexican spice blend has a mild chilli kick, so reduce the amount if you want to avoid the heat.
